translations.text: The book of the birth of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
Abraham fathered Isaac; Isaac fathered Jacob; Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers;
and Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar; and Perez fathered Hezron; and Hezron fathered Ram;
Ram fathered Amminadab; Amminadab fathered Nahshon; Nahshon fathered Salmon;
Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab; Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth; Obed fathered Jesse;
Jesse fathered David the king; David the king fathered Solomon by the wife of Uriah;
Solomon fathered Rehoboam; Rehoboam fathered Abijah; Abijah fathered Asaph;
Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat fathered Joram; Joram fathered Uzziah;
Uzziah fathered Jotham; Jotham fathered Ahaz; Ahaz fathered Hezekiah;
Hezekiah fathered Manasseh; Manasseh fathered Amon; Amon fathered Josiah;
Josiah fathered Jehoiakim; Jehoiakim fathered Jechoniah and his brothers at the time of the Babylonian captivity.
After the Babylonian captivity, Jechoniah fathered Shealtiel; Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel; Zerubbabel fathered Abiud;
Abiud fathered Eliakim; Eliakim fathered Azor;
Azor fathered Zadok; Zadok fathered Achim; Achim fathered Eliud;
Eliud fathered Eleazar; Eleazar fathered Matthan; Matthan fathered Jacob;
Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David were fourteen generations, and from David to the Babylonian captivity fourteen generations, and from the Babylonian captivity to Christ fourteen generations.
Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this: his mother Mary was betrothed to Joseph, and before they came together she was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit.
But Joseph, Mary's husband, was a righteous man and did not want to expose her to disgrace, and he resolved to send her away secretly.

And just as he was considering this, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a vision and said to him: "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary your wife, for what will be born of her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will bear a son, and they shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins."
All this came about so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, who said:
"Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel," which, translated, is: God with us.
Joseph awoke from sleep and did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and he took his wife to himself.
And he did not know her until she bore a son, and they called his name Jesus.
Now when Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of King Herod, behold, magi came from the east to Jerusalem and were saying:
"Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and have come to worship him."
When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
And he gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people and inquired of them: "Where is the Christ to be born?"
And they said to him: "In Bethlehem of Judea, for thus it is written by the prophet:
'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means the least among the rulers of Judah, for from you shall come forth that great ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.'"
Then Herod secretly summoned the magi and learned from them the time of the star's appearing.
And he sent them to Bethlehem and said to them: "Go and search carefully for the child; when you find him, tell me, so that I too may come and worship him."
When they had heard this from the king, they went on their way. And behold, the star which they had seen in the east went before them, until it came and stopped over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
And they came into the house and saw the child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and worshipped him. And they opened their treasures and offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
And they received a command in a dream not to return to Herod; instead they departed by another way and went to their own country.

When they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said to him: "Rise, take the child and his mother, flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod intends to seek out the child to destroy him."
And he rose and set out; he took the child and his mother by night and went to Egypt, and he remained there until the death of Herod,
so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, which says: "Out of Egypt I called my son."

Then when Herod saw that he had been mocked by the magi, he became exceedingly angry, and he sent and killed all the children who were in Bethlehem and in all its borders, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had learned from the magi.
Then was fulfilled what was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, who said:
"A voice was heard in Ramah, of lamentation and weeping and great wailing: Rachel was weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted, because they are no more."
But when Herod had died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt
and said to him: "Rise, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who sought the child's life are dead."
And he rose, took the child and his mother, and came to the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of Herod his father, he was afraid to go there; and having received a command in a dream, he went to the land of Galilee.
And he came and settled in the city called Nazareth, so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: "He shall be called a Nazarene."
In those days John the Baptist came, and he preached in the wilderness of Judea.
And he said: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
For this is the one who was spoken of by Isaiah the prophet, who says: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, and make his paths straight."
John himself wore clothing made of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region around the Jordan went out to him.
And they were baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins.
And when he saw the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to be baptized by him, he said to them: "Brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath to come?"
So now bear fruit worthy of repentance,
and do not think and say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' For I tell you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
For even now the axe lies at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not bear good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one who comes after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not able to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor; he will gather his wheat into the storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire."
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
But John tried to stop him and said to him: "I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?"
Jesus answered and said to him: "Allow it now, for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness." Then at last he permitted him.
And Jesus was baptized, and immediately he came up out of the water. And at once the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.
And behold, there was a voice from heaven, and it said: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
And he fasted forty days and forty nights, and afterward he was hungry.
And the tempter came to him and said to him: "If you are the Son of God, say that these stones should become bread."
But he answered and said: "It is written: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes out of the mouth of God."
Then the devil took him to the holy city and set him on the pinnacle of the temple

and said to him: "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here, for it is written: He has commanded his angels concerning you, and they will bear you up on their hands, lest you strike your foot against a stone."
Jesus said to him: "Again it is written: You shall not tempt the Lord your God."
Again the devil took him up to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms and their glory.
And he said to him: "All this I will give you, if you fall down and worship me."
Then Jesus said to him: "Go away, Satan, for it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve."
Then the devil left him at once, and angels came to him and ministered to him.
Now when Jesus heard that John had been handed over to prison, he went away to Galilee.
And he left Nazareth and came and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the territory of Zebulun and Naphtali,
so that the word spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled:
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles:
the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and on those who sat in the region and shadow of death a light has shone."
From then on Jesus began to preach and to say: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
And as he was walking by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who was called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net, for they were fishermen.
And he said to them: "Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
At once they left the nets and followed him.
And going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
And at once they left the boat and their father and followed him.
And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sickness and every infirmity among the people.

And the report about him went out through all Syria. And they brought to him all the sick, those afflicted with various diseases and torments, the demon-possessed, the lunatics, and the paralytics, and he healed them.
And a great crowd followed him. He healed them.
And when Jesus saw the great crowd, he went up onto the mountain and sat down there. His disciples came to him.
He opened his mouth and taught them, saying:
"Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom [?]
[?] they shall inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst [?]
Bless[ed] [?] in heart [?]
Blessed [?]
[?] and [?] and [?]
[?] before you.
You are the salt of the earth. If the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be salted? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by people.
You are the ligh[t] [?] upon [?]
Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a bushel, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house.
In the same way let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works
[?] the law or the prophets; I did not come to abolish, but to fulfil.
But truly I say to you: until heaven and earth pass away,

If anyone breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches people so, he will be called contemptible (least) in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
But I say to you: unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and the Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not kill; and whoever kills will be liable to judgment.
But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother without cause will be liable to judgment; whoever says to his brother, 'Fool!' will be liable to the council; and [?]
If you are offering your gift on the altar and there remember that your brother has some grievance against you,
leave your gift there before your altar, and go first and be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your sacrifice.

Come to a fair agreement with your adversary quickly, while you are still on the way with him, lest your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the torturer, and you be thrown into prison.
Truly I say to you: you will not come out from there until you have paid even the last paltry penny.
But I say to you: everyone who looks at a woman with lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you, for it is better for you that one of your members should perish, and not that your whole body should fall into Gehenna.

And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you, for it is better for you that one of your members should perish, and not that your whole body should fall into Gehenna.
It has been said: Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.
But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife except on the ground of fornication makes her commit adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not swear falsely, but shall render your oath to the Lord.
But I say to you: do not swear at all, neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God,
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Nor swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.
But let your word be: 'Yes, yes' and 'No, no.' Whatever is more than these is from the devil.
You have heard that it was said: An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.
But I say to you: do not resist evil. Instead, if someone strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other one as well.
And whoever wants to take you to court and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well.
And if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two.
Give to whoever asks of you, and do not turn your face away from whoever wants to borrow from you.
You have heard that it was said: You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.
But I say to you: love your enemies, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who seize you.
So that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven, for he makes his sun rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on sinners.
If you love only those who love you, what reward will you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
And if you greet only your friends, what more are you doing? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
Be perfect, as your Father in heaven is perfect.
But take care with your almsgiving: do not do it before people to be seen by them. Otherwise you will have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
When you give your alms, do not proclaim it before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by people. For they receive their reward from them.
But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your almsgiving may be in secret. And your Father who sees what is hidden will repay you openly.
And when you worship, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to worship in the synagogues and in the marketplaces so that they may be seen by people. Truly I say to you: that is their reward.
But when you worship, go into your inner room, shut your door, and worship your Father in secret. And your Father who sees what is hidden will repay you openly.
And when you pray, do not use many words like the hypocrites, for they think that they will be heard because of their many words.
Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
Pray like this: Our Father who are in heaven, holy be your name,
may your kingdom come, may your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.
Give us today our continual bread,
and forgive us our debts, so that we too may forgive our debtors,
and do not lead us into temptation, O Lord, but deliver us from evil. For yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory forever. Amen.
If you forgive people their trespasses, your Father who is in heaven will forgive you as well.
If you do not forgive people their sins, neither will your Father forgive you your sins.
And when you fast, do not be gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to people as fasting. Truly I tell you, that is their reward.
But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
so that you may not appear to people as fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees what is secret, will reward you.
Do not lay up your treasures on earth, where the moth and the devourer destroy, and where thieves dig through and steal.
But lay up your treasures in heaven, where neither the moth nor the devourer destroys, and where thieves cannot dig through or steal.
For where your treasures are, there also are your hearts.
The lamp of the body is the eye. If your eye is bright, your whole body will be full of light.
If your eye is evil, your whole body will be darkened. If the light that is in you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
No one can serve two masters: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
Therefore I tell you: do not be anxious for yourselves, what you will eat or what you will drink; nor for your bodies [?]
Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow, nor reap, nor gather into storehouses, and your Father who is in heaven feeds them. Are you not better than the birds?
Which of you by being anxious can add one cubit to his stature?
And why are you anxious about clothing? Look at the lilies of the field, how they grow! They do not toil, nor do they spin.
But I tell you: not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
If God so adorns the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, you of little faith?
So do not be anxious, saying: What shall we eat, or what shall we drink, or what shall we wear?
For the gentiles seek all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
Do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for this day is its own trouble.
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged,
and with the judgment with which you judge, with that you will be judged, and with the measure with which you measure out, with that it will be measured to you.
Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye and do not notice the beam in your own eye?
Or how can you say to your brother: Let me take that speck out of your eye, and look, there is a beam in your own eye?
Hypocrite, first take that beam out of your own eye, and then you will see to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor lay your pearl before swine, lest they trample it under their feet and turn and tear you apart.
But ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and whoever knocks, it is opened to him.
And is there any man among you whose son asks him for bread, and will he give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a serpent?
If you, then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give good things to those who ask him.
Whatever you wish that people would do to you, do so to them as well, for this is the Law and the Prophets.
Enter by the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who go by it.
For narrow is the gate and strait is the way that leads to life, and few are those who find it.
But beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves.
By their fruit you will know them. Are grapes gathered from thorns, or figs from thistles?
So every good tree brings forth good fruit, but [?]
A good tree cannot bring forth bad fruit, nor can a tree [?]
Every tree that does not bring forth good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
So then, by their fruit you will know them.
Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord!' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
Many will say to me on that day: 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?'
Then I will say to them: 'I never knew you; depart from me, all you workers of lawlessness.'
Everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house upon the rock.
And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds beat and struck that house, and it did not fall, for it was founded upon that rock.
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house upon the sand.
And the rain came down, and the rivers rose, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell. And great was its fall.
And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, that the crowd was astonished at his teaching.
For he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.
And when he came down from the mountain, a great crowd followed him.
And behold, a leper came before him and bowed down to him and said: Lord, if you will, you are able to cleanse me.
And Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him and said to him: I will; be cleansed! And immediately he was cleansed of his leprosy.
Jesus said to him: Take care, tell no one, but go and show yourself to the priest and offer your sacrifice which Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.
And when he entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, entreating him
and saying: Lord, my servant lies in my house paralyzed, terribly tormented.
And Jesus said to him: I will come and heal him.
The centurion answered and said: Lord, I am not worthy that you should come under my roof; but only speak a word, and my servant will be healed.
For I too am a man, and soldiers are under my command; and I say to this one, 'Go!' and he goes; and to another, 'Come!' and he comes; and I command my slave, 'Do this!' and he does it.
But when Jesus heard this, he marveled and said to those who followed him: Truly I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.
But I tell you: many will come from the east and the west and will recline at table with Abraham, with Isaac and with Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
But the sons of the kingdom will be cast out into the outer darkness. There [?]
And Jesus said to the centurion: Go, and as you have believed, let it be done for you! And his servant was healed on that day.
And Jesus came to Peter's house and saw his mother-in-law lying sick with fever.
And he touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she got up and served him.
And when evening came, they brought to him many who were possessed by demons, and he cast out the spirits with a word and healed all the sick.
So that the word spoken by Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: He took our infirmities upon himself and bore our diseases.
When Jesus saw a great crowd around him, he commanded them to cross over to the other side of the sea.
And a scribe came up and said to him: Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.
And Jesus said to him: Foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.
One of his disciples said to him: Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.
Jesus said to him: Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.
And when he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.
And behold, there was a great storm on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves. But he himself was asleep.
And his disciples came to him, woke him and said to him: Lord, save us, for we are perishing.
And he said to them: Why are you afraid, you of little faith? Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
But the men were amazed and said, "Who is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"

And when he crossed over to the other side, to the country of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men met him, coming out of the tombs. They were extremely fierce, so that no one could pass along that road.
And at once they cried out and said, "What is there between us and you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?"
And some distance from them a large herd of pigs was feeding.
And the demons begged him, saying, "If you cast us out, command us to go into that herd of pigs."
And he said to them, "Go!" And they went into the herd of pigs. And at once the whole herd rushed down the cliff into the sea and perished in the waters.
And the swineherds fled into the city and told everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.
And at once the whole city came out to meet Jesus. And when they saw him, they begged him to leave their region.
And he got into the boat, crossed back over, and came to his own city.
And behold, they brought to him a paralytic, lying on a bed. And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, "Do not be afraid, child; your sins are forgiven!"
And at once some of the scribes said within their hearts, "This man is blaspheming."
And when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he said to them, "Why do you think evil in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven you,' or to say, 'Rise and walk'?
For the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive their sins." Then he said to the paralytic, "Rise, take up your bed, and go to your house!"
And he rose and went to his house.
When the crowd saw it, they were amazed, and they glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
And as Jesus was going on from there, he saw a man sitting at the tax booth, named Matthew, and he said to him, "Follow me." And he rose and followed him.
And it happened that as he was reclining at table in the house, many tax collectors and sinners had come and were reclining at table with Jesus and with his disciples.
And when the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
But when Jesus heard it, he said to them, "Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those who are sick.
Go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.' For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
Then the disciples of John came to him and said to him, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast much, but your disciples do not fast?"
And Jesus said to them, "Can the children of the wedding mourn while the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
No one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, for the patch tears away from the garment, and a worse tear is made.
Nor do they pour new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst, the wine is spilled, and the wineskins are destroyed. But they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved."

While he was saying this to them, behold, a certain ruler came to him, bowed down before him and said to him: "My daughter has just now, behold, died; but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live."
And Jesus rose and followed him, and his disciples with him.
And behold, a certain woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years came up from behind and touched the hem of his garment.
For she said in her heart: "If I only touch his garment, I will be made well."
But Jesus turned, saw her and said to her: "Do not be afraid, daughter! Your faith has made you well." And the woman was made well from that hour.
And when Jesus came to the ruler's house, he saw the flute-players there and the crowd in an uproar,
and he said to them: "Go away, for this girl has not died, but is sleeping." And they mocked him.
But when they had put the crowd out, he went in and took her by the hand, and the girl rose up.
And this report about him went out into all that land.
And as Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying: "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"
And when he had gone into the house, the blind men came to him, and Jesus said to them: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" They said to him: "Yes, Lord."
Then he touched their eyes and said: "According to your faith, let it be done to you!"
And their eyes were opened. And Jesus sternly warned them and said: "See to it that no one finds out!"
But they went out and spread the news about him through all that land.
And as they were going out, behold, they brought to him a deaf man possessed by a demon.
And when the demon had left him, the deaf man spoke, and the crowd was amazed and said: "Never has anyone appeared like this in Israel."
But the Pharisees said: "By the prince of demons he casts out demons."
And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and infirmity among the people.
And when he saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, for they were weary and scattered, like sheep that have no shepherd.
Then he said to his disciples: "The harvest is great, but the workers are few.
Pray to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out workers into his harvest."
And he called his twelve disciples to him and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every disease and every infirmity.
Now these are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon, who was called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James son of Zebedee and John his brother;
Philip [?]
Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
Jesus sent out these twelve. He instructed them and said to them: "Do not go on the road of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans.
Go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
And as you go, preach and say: 'The kingdom of heaven has come near.'
Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons. You have received without payment; give without payment as well.
Do not acquire gold, or silver, or copper for your belts,
no bag for the road, no two tunics, no sandals, no staff, for the worker is worthy of his food.
Whatever city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you leave.
And when you enter a house, greet it and say: 'Peace to this house!'
If that house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
And whoever does not receive you or listen to your words, when you leave that house or city, shake the dust off your feet.
Truly I tell you: it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.
Behold, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. So be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.
But beware of people, for they will hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues.
And they will bring you before judges and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
But when they hand you over, do not worry about how or what you are to speak, for what you are to say will be given to you at that hour.
For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
For brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child; and children will rise up against their parents and kill them.
And you will be hated by all because of my name. But whoever endures to the end will be saved.

When they persecute you in this city, flee to another. And if they persecute you there too, flee from there to the next. Truly I tell you: you will not finish going through the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.
It is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher, and the servant like his master. If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they call the members of his household so?
Do not be afraid of them, for there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor any secret that will not come to light.
What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear in your ears, proclaim upon the rooftops.
And do not be afraid of those who kill your bodies but are unable to kill your souls. Rather, fear him who is able to destroy souls together with bodies in Gehenna.
Are not two sparrows sold for one danga [a small coin]? Yet not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father.
But even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
So do not be afraid, for you are better than many sparrows.
Everyone who confesses me before people, I too will confess him before my Father who is in heaven.
But whoever denies me before people, I too will deny him before my Father who is in heaven.
Do not think that I have come to bring peace on earth. I have not come to bring peace, but a sword.
For I have come to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
And a man's enemies will be the members of his own household.
Whoever loves his father or his mother more than me is not worthy of me; and whoever loves his son or his daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.
Whoever finds his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.

Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward; and whoever receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person's reward.
And whoever gives one of these little ones even a single cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward.
And it happened that when Jesus had finished giving these instructions to his twelve disciples, he went on from there to teach and to preach in their cities.
Now John, in prison, heard of the works of Christ, and he sent [?]
and said to him: "Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?"
Jesus answered and said to them: "Go and tell John what you hear and see:
the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the afflicted have good news brought to them.
And blessed is the one who does not stumble because of me."
As they were leaving, Jesus began to speak about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
What then did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Look, those who wear soft clothing are in the houses of kings.
What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
For this is the one about whom it is written: 'Behold, I send my angel before your face, and he will prepare your way before you.'
Truly I tell you: among those born of women no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven is taken by force, and the violent seize it.
For all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John.
And if you are willing to accept it, he himself is Elijah, who is to come.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
To what shall I liken this generation? It is like children sitting in the streets, who call out to their companions
and say: We piped for you, and you did not dance; we mourned for you, and you did not beat your breasts.
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say: He is possessed by a demon.
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say: Look, a glutton and a drinker of wine, a friend of tax collectors and of sinners! And wisdom has been justified by her children.
Then Jesus began to reproach the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done, because they did not repent:

Woe to you, Chorazin, and woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works that were done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would [?] have repented then and there, sitting in sackcloth on ashes.
But I tell you: it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? No, you will go down to hell. For if the mighty works that were done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained to this very day.
For I tell you: it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for you.

At that time Jesus spoke and said: I give thanks to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the learned and have revealed them to little children.
Yes, Father, for so it was pleasing in your sight.
All things have been given to me by my Father; and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.
Come to me, all you who are weary and who carry heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
For my yoke is sweet and my burden is light.
At that time Jesus was going through their grainfields on the Sabbath day. His disciples were hungry, and they began to pluck heads of grain and eat.
When the Pharisees saw this, they said to him: Look, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.
But he said to them: Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him?
How he entered the house of God and ate the bread of the offering, which was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests?
Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are blameless?
But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
If you had known what this means, 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned the blameless.
For the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.
And Jesus went on from there and came into their synagogue.
And there was a man there whose hand was withered. And they questioned him, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?" so that they might accuse him.
But Jesus said to them, "Which man among you who has one sheep, if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out?
How much better, then, is a man than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath."
Then he said to the man, "Stretch out your hand!" And he stretched it out, and it was restored to life, like the other one.
But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him. And Jesus, when he perceived it, went away from there.
And many crowds followed him, and he healed them all.
And he sternly warned them not to make him known,
so that the word spoken by Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
"Behold, here is my son, whom I have chosen, in whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my spirit upon him, and he will proclaim judgments to the Gentiles.
He will not quarrel, nor cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets.
A bruised reed he will not break, and a burning wick he will not quench, until he brings forth judgment to victory.
And in his name the Gentiles will hope."
Then they brought to him a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute, and he healed him, so that the mute and blind man both spoke and saw.
And all the crowd was amazed, and they said, "Could this be the Christ, the son of David?"
But when the Pharisees saw it, they said, "This man casts out the demons by nothing other than Beelzebul, the prince of the demons."
When Jesus knew their thoughts, he said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
And if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand?
If I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
If I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Or how can anyone enter a strong man's house and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man, and only then plunders his house?
Whoever is not with me is my enemy, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
Therefore I tell you: every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
And if anyone speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the one to come.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad; for the tree is known by its fruit.
You offspring of vipers, how can you speak good things? For you are evil, because the mouth speaks out of the abundance of the heart.
The good man brings forth good out of his good treasure, and the evil man brings forth evil out of his evil treasure.
But I say to you: for every idle word that men speak, they will give account for it on the day of judgment.
For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.
Then some of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered him and said to him: Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.
But he answered them and said to them: An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea monster three days and three nights, so will the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, lo, one greater than Jonah is here.

The queen of the south will rise up at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
But when the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it passes through waterless places, seeking a place of rest, and does not find it.
Then it says: I will return to my house from which I came out. And it comes and finds it empty, set in order, adorned, and decorated.

Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they come and dwell there. And the last state of that person becomes worse than the first. So it will be also with this evil generation.
And while he was still speaking to the crowd, behold, lo, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to him.
Then someone said to him: Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing outside and want to say something to you.
But Jesus answered the one who spoke and said to him: Who is my mother, or who are my brothers?
And he stretched out his hand toward his disciples and said: Behold, my mother and my brothers!
For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, that one is brother, sister, and mother.
On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the seashore.
And a great crowd gathered to him, so that he got into a boat and sat down. And the whole crowd stood on the seashore.
And he spoke many things to them in parables and said to them: Behold, a sower went out to sow.
And as he sowed, some fell on the path, and the birds of the sky came and ate it.
And other seed fell on rock, where there was not much soil; and it sprang up at once, because there was no depth of soil.
The sun rose and scorched it, and because it had not put down roots, it withered.
And other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns sprang up and choked it.
And some fell on good ground and yielded fruit: some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, and some thirtyfold.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
And the disciples came to him and said to him, "Why do you speak to them in parables?"
And Jesus said to them, "Because to you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.
For whoever has, to him it will be given, and more will be added; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
This is why I speak to them in parables: because they see and do not see, and they hear and do not hear, nor do they understand.
And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah the prophet, which says: 'Hearing you will hear and not understand, and seeing you will see and not perceive.

For the heart of this people has grown fat, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart, and turn, and be healed.'
But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
Amen, I say to you, many prophets and righteous men longed in their hearts to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.
Now hear, then, the parable of the sower.
Whenever anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the one that was sown along the road.
And the one that was sown on rocky ground is this: the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.
But he has no root in his heart, and lasts only for a while. So when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he immediately stumbles.
And the one that was sown among the thorns is this: the one who hears the word, and the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And the one that was sown on the good ground is this: the one who hears the word and understands it, and bears fruit and yields, one a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, another thirtyfold."
He set another parable before them and said: "The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
And while the men were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed darnel among the wheat and went away.
So when the blade sprang up and bore fruit, then the darnel also appeared.
And the servants of the householder came and said to him, 'Lord, did you not sow good seed in this field of yours? Where then does this darnel come from?'
And he said to them, 'An enemy has done this.' The servants said to him, 'Do you want us to go and weed it out?'
But he said to them, 'No, lest in weeding out the darnel you uproot the wheat along with it.
Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will command the reapers: Gather the darnel first and bind it in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my storehouse.'"
He told them another parable and said: "The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field,
which is the smallest of all seeds, but when it has grown it is greater than all the herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of heaven come and settle in its branches."
He told them another parable: "The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened."
Jesus told the people all these things in parables, and he told them nothing without a parable,
so that the word spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: "I will open my mouth in parables, and I will speak of things hidden since the creation of the world."
Then Jesus left the people and came to his house. His disciples came to him and said, "Explain to us the parable of the tares and the field."
He answered them and said, "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is this kingdom. The good seed are the children of the kingdom, and the tares are the children of the evil one.
The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of this world, and the reapers are angels.
Just as they gather the tares and burn them with fire, so it will be at the end of this world.
For the Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all causes of stumbling and those who do lawlessness,
and they will throw them into the furnace of burning fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of heaven. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid. In his joy he went and sold everything he had and bought that field.
Then the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant who was looking for fine pearls.
When he found one very costly pearl, he went and sold everything he had and bought it.
Then again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that is cast into the sea and gathers fish of every kind.
When it is full, they draw it up onto the shore, sit down, sort them, and gather the good into a vessel, but they throw the bad away.
So it will be at the end of this world: the angels will go out and separate the wicked from the righteous,
and they will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there.
"Have you understood all this?" They said to him, "Yes, Lord."
And he said to them, "Therefore every scribe who has become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven is like the master of a household who brings out of his treasure things new and old."
And when Jesus had finished these parables, he went away from there.
He came to his own country and taught them in their synagogues. They were amazed and said, "Where did this man get this wisdom and these powers?
Is this not the carpenter's son? Is his mother not called Mary, and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
And are not all his sisters here with us? Where did this man get all this?"
And they took offence at him. But Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honour except in his own country and in his own house."
And he did not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
At that time Herod the [?] (tetrarch?) heard the report about Jesus,
and he said to his servants: "This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work through him."
For Herod had earlier seized John, bound him and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.
For John had been telling him: "It is not lawful for you to have her as your wife."
And although he wanted to kill him, he feared the people, because they regarded him as a prophet.
But when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced among them, and her dancing pleased Herod,
so that he promised with an oath to give her whatever she might ask.
And she, having been prompted beforehand by her mother, said: "Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
And although the king was grieved, because of the oath and those reclining at table with him, he commanded that it be given to her.
And he sent and had John beheaded in the prison.
And they brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
And his disciples came and took away his body and buried it, and they came and told Jesus.
Now when Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there by boat and went from there to a desolate place by himself. And when the crowd heard of it, they followed him [?] (on foot?) from the towns.
And Jesus came out and saw a great crowd, and he had compassion on them and healed their sick.

And when evening came, his disciples came to him and said to him: "This place is desolate, and the hour is already past; send this crowd away, so that they may go into the surrounding villages and buy food for themselves."
But Jesus said to them: "They do not need to go away; you give them something to eat."
And they said to him: "We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish."
And he said to them: "Bring them here to me!"

And he ordered the crowd to sit down on the grass. And he took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, and gave the bread to his disciples, and the disciples gave it to the crowd.
And they all ate and were satisfied; and they took up what was left of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full.
And those who ate were about five thousand men, besides children and women.
And immediately he made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the crowd away.
And when he had sent the crowd away, he went up on the mountain by himself to pray. And when evening came, he was there alone.
But the boat was by then many stadia away from land, and it was being battered by the waves, for the wind was against them.
And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus came to them, walking.
But when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were terrified and said, "It is some apparition." And they cried out for fear.
At once Jesus spoke to them and said, "Take courage! It is I; do not be afraid!"
Peter answered and said to him, "Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on these waters."
And he said, "Come!" And Peter got down from the boat, walked on the waters, and came to Jesus.
And when he saw the strong wind, he was afraid and began to sink, and he cried out and said, "Lord, save me!"
At once Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and said, "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"
And when they had gone up into the boat, the wind ceased.
And those who were in the boat came to him and worshipped him and said, "Truly you are the Son of God."
And they crossed over and came to the land of Gennesaret.
And the men of that place recognized him and sent word into all that surrounding region, and they brought to him all who were grievously afflicted.
And they begged him that they might only touch the hem of his garment. And those who touched it were made whole.
Then Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem came to Jesus and said to him,
"Why do your disciples transgress the teaching of the priests? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."
He answered and said to them, "Why do you also transgress the commandment of God for the sake of your teaching?
For God said, 'Honor your father and mother'; and, 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother, let him surely die.'
But you say, 'Whoever says to his father or his mother, "Whatever benefit you would have had from me is a gift,"
and does not honor his father' — and so you have made the word of God of no account for the sake of your teaching.
Hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy about you when he said:
'This people honors me only with their lips, but their heart is far removed from me.
In vain do they worship me, for they teach the doctrines and commandments of men.'"
And he called the crowd to him and said to them, "Hear and understand!
It is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth, that is what defiles a person."
Then the disciples came and said to him, "Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard your saying?"
But he answered and said to them, "Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted.
But leave them alone: they are blind, and leaders of the blind. And if a blind man leads a blind man, they go astray, and both fall into the pit.
Peter answered and said to him: Explain this parable to us.
And Jesus said to him: Now, are you also still without understanding?
And do you not know that everything that enters by the mouth goes into the belly and goes out through the outlet?
But what comes out of the mouth comes out of the heart, and that defiles a man.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, slanders, blasphemies.
These are what defile a man; but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a man.
And Jesus went out from there and came to the regions of Tyre and Sidon.
And a Canaanite woman came out from those borders, crying out and saying: Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David, for my daughter is grievously possessed by a demon.
But he himself did not answer her a word. And his disciples came to him and spoke to him and said: Send her away, for she is following us and crying out.
And Jesus said to them: I have not been sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
But she came to him, worshipped him, and said to him: Lord, have mercy on me!
And he himself answered and said to her: It is not good to take the bread from the children and to put it before the dogs.
And she said: Yes, Lord, for even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.
Then Jesus answered and said to her: O woman! Great is your faith; let it be done to you as you wish. And her daughter was healed from that hour.
And Jesus went out from there and came to the shore of the Sea of Galilee, went up onto the mountain, and sat down there.

And a great crowd came to him, who had with them the lame and the blind, the deaf and the crippled, and many others seized by diseases of various kinds; and they laid them at Jesus' feet, and he healed them.

So that the crowd was amazed when they saw how the deaf and the mute were speaking, and the lame were walking, and the crippled were being healed, and the blind were seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.

And Jesus called his disciples and said to them: I have compassion on this crowd, for now, behold, it is three days that they have been waiting for me, and they have nothing to eat; and I do not want to send them away fasting, lest they collapse on the way.
And his disciples said to him: Where are we to get so much bread in the wilderness, so as to feed so great a crowd?
And Jesus said to them: How many loaves do you have here? And they said: Seven loaves and a few fish.
And he commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground.
And he took the seven loaves and the fish, and gave thanks, and broke them, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowd.
And they all ate and were satisfied; and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces, seven baskets full.
And those who ate were four thousand men, besides children and women.
And he sent them away, went up into the boat, and came to the borders of Magdala.
And the Pharisees and Sadducees came to him, testing him and questioning him, so that he would show them a sign from heaven.
But he answered and said to them: "When evening comes, you say, 'It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.'
And in the morning you say, 'There will be a storm today, for the sky is red and overcast.' Hypocrites! You know how to read the face of the sky, but you cannot understand the signs of the times.
An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet." And he left them and went away.
And his disciples came, and they had forgotten to take bread.
And Jesus said to them: "Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
But they reasoned in their hearts and said: "We have no bread."
When Jesus perceived it, he said to them: "Why do you reason in your hearts, you of little faith, saying, 'We have no bread'?
Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand?
How is it that you do not understand that I did not speak to you about bread when I said, 'Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees'?"
Then they understood that he had not told them to beware of leaven, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
And Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, and he asked his disciples, saying: "Who do people say that I, the Son of Man, am?"
And they said: "Some say John the Baptist, some Elijah, and some Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
He said to them: "But who do you say that I am?"
Simon Peter answered and said: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
Jesus answered and said to him: "Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.
And I also say to you that you are the rock, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven."
Then he commanded the disciples to tell no one that he was Jesus the Christ.

From that time Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes, and be killed, and be raised on the third day.
And Peter came to him and began to rebuke him, saying: "Mercy on you, Lord! May this not happen!"
He turned to Peter and said to him: "Get behind me, Satan, for you are a stumbling block to me, for you are not thinking the things of God, but the things of men."
Then Jesus said to his disciples: "Whoever wishes to follow after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me."
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
What profit will a man have if he gains the world and loses his own soul? Or what will a man give in exchange for his soul?
For the Son of Man is to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each person according to their deeds.
Truly I tell you, there are some of those standing here who will not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.
And after the sixth day Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.
And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothing became white as the light.
And at once Moses and Elijah appeared to them, and they were talking with him.
Peter answered and said to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here. And if you wish, let us make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
And while he was still saying this, behold, a cloud of light overshadowed them, and at once a voice came out of the cloud and said: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him!
And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their faces and were greatly afraid.
And Jesus came to them, touched them with his hand, and said: Get up, do not be afraid!
And when they lifted up their eyes, they saw no one but Jesus alone.
And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying: Tell no one about the vision until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.
And the disciples asked him, saying: Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?
And he answered and said: Elijah is to come and will restore all things.
But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of Man is to suffer at their hands.
Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist.
And when they came to the crowd, a certain man came up to him, knelt down, and said to him:
Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is a lunatic and suffers terribly; for he often falls into the fire and often into the water.
And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not heal him.
Jesus answered and said to them: O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him here to me!
And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon went out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour.
Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said to him: Why could we not drive it out?

And he said to them: Because of your little faith. For truly I tell you, if you have faith even as a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain: Move from here! and it will move there. And nothing will be impossible for you.
And while they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them: The Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of men,
and they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise. And they were greatly grieved.
And when they came to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma came to Peter and said to him: "Does your teacher not pay the drachma tax?"

And he said to them: "Yes." And as he went into the house, Jesus spoke first and said to him: "What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth take tax or toll: from their sons or from strangers?"
He said to him: "From strangers." Jesus said to him: "Then the sons are free."

"But so that we do not cause them to stumble, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the fish that comes up first, and open its mouth, and you will find a stater in it. Take it and give it to them for me and for you."
On that day the disciples came to Jesus and said: "Who is greater in the kingdom of heaven?"
And Jesus called a child and set him among them,
and said to them: "Truly I tell you: unless you turn and become like children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
For whoever humbles himself like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever receives one such child in my name receives me.

But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a donkey-driven millstone were hung around his neck and he were cast into the depths of the seas.
Woe to this world because of stumbling blocks, for stumbling blocks are bound to come; but woe to the man through whom the stumbling block comes.

If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life lame or without a hand than to have two hands or two feet and fall into the eternal fire.
And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and fall into the Gehenna of fire.
But take care that you do not despise one of these little ones. I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.
For the Son of Man came to save what was lost.
What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountain and go and look for the one that went astray?
And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
In the same way, it is not the will of my Father in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him while you and he are alone. If he listens to you, you have won back your brother.
If he does not listen to you, take one or two others with you, so that every word may be confirmed by the mouth of two or three witnesses.
If he does not listen to them either, tell the church; and if he does not listen to the church either, let him be to you like a gentile and a tax collector.
Truly I tell you: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven."
Again, truly I say to you: if two of you agree on earth about any matter, whatever they ask will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.
For where two or three are gathered together for my name's sake, there I am among them.
Then Peter came to him and said to him: "Lord, how many times shall my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?"
Jesus said to him: "I do not say to you up to seven times, but seventy times seven times."
Therefore the kingdom of heaven is like a man, a king, who wished to settle accounts with his servants.
And when he began to settle accounts, they brought before him one who owed ten thousand talents.
And since he had nothing with which to pay, his lord commanded that he be sold, along with his wife, his children and everything he had, and that payment be made.
The servant fell down, bowed before him and said to him: "Be patient with me, and I will pay you everything."
The lord had pity on that servant, released him, and forgave him the debt.
And when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He seized him and began choking him, saying to him: "Pay me what you owe."
His fellow servant fell down, begged him and said to him: "Be patient with us, and I will pay you."
But he refused; instead he went and threw him into prison until he should pay the debt.
So when his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly grieved. They came and told their lord everything that had happened.
His lord summoned him and said to him: "Wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you begged me.
Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?"
And his lord was angry and handed him over to the torturers until he should pay everything he owed him.
So also will my heavenly Father do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts.
And when Jesus had finished these words, he set out from Galilee and came to the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.
Great crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
And Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying to him: "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?"
He answered and said to them: "Have you not read that he who created them in the beginning made them male and female? And he said:
'For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.'
From then on they are no longer two but one flesh. Therefore, what God has joined together, let no man separate."
They said to him: "Why then did Moses command us to give a certificate of divorce and divorce her?"
He said to them: "Because of your hardness of heart Moses allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it was not so."
Amen, I tell you: everyone who leaves his wife, except for fornication, and marries another, commits adultery; and whoever marries a woman who has been put away commits adultery.
His disciples said to him: "If this is how a man's case stands with a woman, it is better not to take a wife."
But he said to them: "Not everyone can accept this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.

For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb; and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Whoever is able to accept this, let him accept it."
Then children were brought to him, so that he might lay his hand on them and bless them. And the disciples rebuked them.
But Jesus said to them: "Let those children be, and do not hinder them from coming to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."
And he laid his hand on them and went away from there.
And behold, someone came up to him and said: "Good teacher, what good thing should I do so that I may have eternal life?"
But he said to him: "Why do you ask me about goodness? One is good. If you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments."
He said to him: "Which ones?" He said: "You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, nor bear false witness.
Honor your father and mother, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself."
The young man said to him: "I have kept all these from my youth; what do I still lack?"
Jesus said to him: "If you wish to be perfect, go and sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will gain treasure in heaven; and come, follow me."
But when the young man heard this saying, he went away grieving, for he was very wealthy.
And Jesus said to his disciples: "Truly, in truth I tell you, a rich man will enter the kingdom of heaven with difficulty.
Again I tell you: it is easier for a rope [?] to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
When his disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and said: "Who then can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them and said to them: "With men this is impossible, but with God everything is possible."
Then Peter answered and said to him: "Behold, we have left everything and followed you; what then will there be for us?"

And Jesus said to them: "Truly I tell you, you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory, you also, the twelve, will sit on thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields for the sake of my name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first.
For the kingdom of heaven is like a man, a householder, who went out at dawn to hire laborers for his vineyard.
And he agreed with the laborers on a stater a day and sent them into his vineyard.
And he came out at about the third hour and saw others standing idle in the marketplace,
And he said to them, "You go into my vineyard too, and whatever is right I will give you."
And they went. Then he went out at the sixth and the ninth hour, and did the same.
And when he went out at the eleventh hour, he found others standing there, and he said to them, "Why do you stand here idle all day?"
They said to him, "Because no one has hired us." He said to them, "You go into my vineyard too."
When evening came, the lord of the vineyard said to his steward, "Call the workers and give them their wages; begin with the last and go on to the first."
So when those of the eleventh hour came, they each received a denarius.
And when the first came, they thought that they would receive more; but they too each received a denarius.
And when they received it, they grumbled against the householder,
and said, "These last ones worked only one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and the heat."
But he answered one of them and said, "Friend, I am not cheating you. Did I not promise you a denarius?"
"And if I wish to give to this last one the same as to you,
am I not allowed to do what I want with what is mine? Is your eye evil, while I am generous?"
So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.
And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve aside by themselves, and on the way he said to them:
"Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death.
And they will hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and scourged and crucified, and on the third day he will rise again."
Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, bowing down and asking something of him.
And he said to her, "What do you want?" And she said to him, "Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom."

Jesus answered and said to her, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, and to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?" They said to him, "We are able."

Jesus said to them, "You will drink my cup, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized; but to sit at my right hand is not mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father."
And when the ten heard it, they became indignant at the two brothers.
But Jesus called them and said to them, "You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and the rich exercise authority over them.
But it is not so among you; rather, whoever wishes to be great among you, let him be your servant;
and whoever wants to be first among you, let him be your slave;
just as the Son of Man did not come to be served by anyone, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many."
And as they were going out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him.
And two blind men were sitting by the road. They heard that Jesus was passing by, and they cried out and said: Have mercy on us, Jesus, Son of David!
But the crowd rebuked them, so that they would be silent. They cried out all the more and said: Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!
And Jesus stopped, called to them, and said to them: What do you want me to do for you?
They said to him: Lord, that our eyes may be opened.
Jesus had pity on them and touched their eyes, and at once their eyes were opened, and they followed him.
And when they drew near to Jerusalem and he came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two of his disciples
and said to them: Go into the village that is opposite you, and at once you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with it. Untie them and bring them to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, you shall say: Their lord needs them. And at once they will send them.
Now all this happened so that the word spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled:
Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, here your king is coming to you; he is meek and is seated upon a donkey and upon a colt of a donkey.
And the disciples went and did as Jesus had commanded them.
And they brought the donkey and the colt, and they laid garments on it, and he sat on it.
And the great crowd of people spread their garments on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
And the crowds that went before him and that followed behind were crying out and saying: Glorified is the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, and glorified in the highest!
And when he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and said: Who is this?
And the crowd said: This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.

And Jesus went into the temple and drove out all who were selling and buying in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the [?] sellers (literally "seed-sellers"; probably the money-changers) and the seats of those who were selling doves.
And he said to them: It is written: My house shall be called a house of worship; but you have made it a den of robbers.
And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
When the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonders that he had done, and the children who were crying out in the temple and saying: Glory to the Son of David,
they became angry and said to him: Do you hear what these are saying? And Jesus said to them: Have you never read: Out of the mouth of infants and sucklings you have established praise?
He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, and stayed there.
In the morning, as he was going up to the city, he became hungry.
And he saw a fig tree by the road, and he came to it and found nothing on it but leaves only, and he said to it: May fruit never again come from you, forever! And at once the fig tree withered.
When the disciples saw this, they were amazed and said, "How did this fig tree wither so suddenly?"

Jesus answered and said to them, "Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to this fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Rise up and throw yourself into the sea,' it will happen.
