And whatever you ask in prayer with faith will be given to you."

And when he came into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him while he was teaching and said to him, "By what authority do you do these things, and who gave you this authority?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "I too will ask you one question, and if you tell me, I too will tell you by what authority I do these things.

The baptism of John, where was it from? Was it from heaven or from men?" And they reasoned in their hearts, saying, "If we say, 'It was from heaven,' he will say to us, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
If we say, 'It was from men,' we are afraid of the people, for all hold John to be a prophet."
And they answered Jesus and said to him, "We do not know." He also said to them, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
What do you think? A certain man had two sons. He came to the first and said, 'Son, go today and work in my vineyard.'
And he answered and said, 'I will go, lord,' and he did not go.
And he went to the other one and said the same. And he answered and said, 'I do not want to.' But afterward he repented and went.

Which of the two did the will of his father?" They said to him, "The last." Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the kingdom of God.

For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and you, even when you saw it, did not repent afterward so as to believe him.
Hear another parable: There was a certain man, a householder, who planted a vineyard and put a fence around it, and dug a winepress in it, and built a tower, and leased it to tenants and went away.
And when the season of fruit drew near, he sent his servants to those tenants to receive his fruit.
And the tenants seized his servants; one they beat, others they killed, and another they stoned.
Then he sent other servants, more than the first, and they did the same to them as well.
Last of all he sent his son to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
But when those tenants saw his son, they plotted among themselves: 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him and seize his inheritance.'
And they seized him and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
So when the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?"
They said to him, "He will miserably destroy those wicked men and will give the vineyard to other tenants, who will give him the fruit in their seasons."
Jesus said to them, "Have you never read in the Scriptures: 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; this was from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?
Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a people that produces its fruits.
And whoever falls on that stone will be broken to pieces, and on whomever it falls, it will crush him to powder."
When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they understood whom he was speaking about.
They sought to seize him, but they feared the people, because the people regarded him as a prophet.
Jesus answered again and spoke to them in a parable:
"The kingdom of heaven is like a king who held a wedding feast for his son.
He sent his servants to call those who had been invited to the wedding, but they would not come.

Again he sent other servants and said, 'Tell those who have been invited: Behold, I have prepared my dinner, my oxen and my fatted calves have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to this wedding feast.'
But they paid no attention and went away, one to his own farm, another to his business,
and the rest seized his servants and killed them.
The king was angry. He sent his troops, destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
Then he said to his servants, 'The wedding feast is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy.
So go out to the crossroads and invite to this wedding feast as many as you find.'
The servants went out into the roads and gathered all they found, both bad and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
When the king came in to look at the guests, he saw there a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.
He said to him, 'Friend, how did you come in here without wearing wedding clothes?' But the man was speechless.
Then the king said to the attendants, 'Bind his feet and hands and throw him out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there.'
For many are called, but few are chosen."
Then the Pharisees went and plotted against him, how they might trap him in his words.

They sent their disciples to him together with the Herodians, and they said, "Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and you are not concerned about anyone, because you do not look at a person's face.
So tell us, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay tax to Caesar, or not?"
Jesus perceived their wickedness and said, "Why are you testing me, you hypocrites?
Show me the coin for the tax." They brought him a denarius.
Jesus said to them, "Whose image and inscription is this?"
They said to him, "Caesar's." Then he said to them, "Then give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
When they heard this, they were amazed, and they left him and went away.
That same day the Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him. They questioned him
And they said to him: "Teacher, Moses said: 'If someone dies childless, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.'
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first husband died, and since he had no child, he left his wife to his brother.
So also the second and the third, down to the seventh.
Last of all, the woman died.
In the resurrection at the last, whose wife of the seven will she be? For all of them had her."
Jesus answered and said to them: "You are wrong, and you know neither the Scripture nor the power of God.
For in the resurrection they neither take wives nor go to husbands, but they are like angels in heaven.
Concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God, who said:
'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living."
And when the crowd heard this, they were astonished at his teaching.
But when the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.
And one of them, a lawyer, asked him in order to test him:
"Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?"
And he said to him: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind.
This is the great and first commandment.
And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbour as yourself.
On these two commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets."
All the Pharisees were gathered together. Jesus asked them
and said: "What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?" They said to him: "David's."
He said to them: "How then does David, in the Spirit, call him Lord, saying:
'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies under your feet'?
If David calls him Lord, how is he his son?"
And no one was able to answer him, nor did anyone dare from that time on to ask him anything more.
Then Jesus spoke to the crowd and to his disciples
and said: "The scribes and the Pharisees sit on the seats of Moses.
Do and keep everything they tell you, but do not act according to their deeds, for they speak and do not do.
They tie up heavy burdens that are hard to carry and lay them on people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to move them even with their finger.
They do all their deeds to be seen by people: they make their garments broad and lengthen their fringes.
They love the place of honor [?] at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues,
and greetings in the marketplaces, and being called by people "Teacher!"
But as for you, do not call yourselves teacher, for one is your Teacher, and you are all brothers.
And call no one on earth your father, for one is your Father, the heavenly one.
And do not call yourselves teacher, for one is your Teacher, the Christ.
And whoever is great among you, let him be your servant.
For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
But woe to you, scribes and hypocritical interpreters, for you shut the kingdom of heaven in people's faces; you do not go in yourselves, nor do you let those who are going in enter.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you travel over sea and dry land to convert a single person; and when he is converted, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves.
Woe to you, blind scribes, for you say: "Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold that is in the temple is bound by his oath."
Fools and blind! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold?
And: "Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the offering that is on it is bound by his oath."
Fools and blind! Which is greater: the offering, or the altar that sanctifies the offering?
So whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything that is on it.
And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who dwells in it.
And whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one who sits on it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you tithe mint, dill and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.
Blind guides, who strain out the gnat and swallow the camel!
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, for you clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of plunder and impurity.
Blind Pharisees, first clean the inside of the cup, so that its outside may also be clean.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but inside are full of dead men's bones and of every impurity.
In the same way you also appear to people outwardly as those who fast, but inside you are full of deceit and lawlessness.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the graves of the righteous.
And you say: "If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have shared with them in the blood of the prophets."
So you testify against yourselves that you are the offspring of those who killed the prophets.
You too, then, fill up the measure of your fathers.
Serpents, offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?
Therefore, behold, I will send you prophets and wise men, scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will flog in your synagogues and hunt down from city to city,
so that all the righteous blood shed on the earth may come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.
Truly I tell you, all this will come upon this generation.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who killed the prophets and stoned those sent to you! How many times I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing!
Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
But I tell you: from now on you will not see me again until you say, "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord."
And Jesus came out of the temple and was going away. And his disciples came up to him to show him the buildings of the temple.
But he answered and said to them: "Do you see all this? Truly I tell you: not one stone will be left here upon another that will not be thrown down."
While he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him privately and said: "Tell us, when will this be, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of this world?"
Jesus answered and said to them: "Take care that no one leads you astray,
for many will come in my name and say, 'I am the Christ,' and they will lead many astray.
And when you hear of wars and the noise of battles, be on your guard and do not be alarmed, for all this must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and pestilences and earthquakes in place after place.
But all this will be the beginning of the birth pangs.
Then they will hand you over to affliction and will kill you, and you will be hated by all nations for the sake of my name.
And then many will go astray, and they will [? betray] one another and hate one another.
And many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.
And because lawlessness will increase, the love of many will grow cold.
But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.
But when you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand),
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains;
and let those who are on the rooftops not come down to take anything from their house;
and let whoever is out in the field not turn back to take his garment.
But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
But pray that your flight may not be in winter, nor on the Sabbath.
For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will be.
And if those days were not shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ' — or 'There he is' — do not believe it.
For false prophets will arise and will perform great miracles and signs, so as to lead astray, if they could, even the elect.
Behold, I have told you beforehand.
If they say to you, 'Look, he is in the wilderness,' do not go out; 'Look, he is in the inner rooms,' do not believe it.
For as the lightning flashes forth from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
For wherever the carcass falls, there the vultures will gather.
Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts in mourning, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
And he will send out his angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
But from the fig tree learn this parable: when its branches become tender and its leaves bud forth, know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.
Truly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
But of that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father alone.
As the days of Noah were, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
For as they were in those days before the flood: they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the very day on which Noah entered the ark,
and they did not know until the flood came and swept them all away. So will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Then two will be in the field: one will be taken and one will be left.
Two will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and one will be left.
Keep watch, for you do not know on what day your Lord will come.
But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief would come, he would not have let his house be broken into.
Therefore you too must be ready, for the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has set over his household to give them their ration at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whose lord, when he comes, finds him doing so.
Truly I tell you, he will set him over all that he has.
But if that wicked servant says in his heart, 'My lord is delaying his coming,'
and begins to beat his fellow servants, and eats and drinks with drunkards,
the lord of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know,
and will cut him in pieces and assign him his portion with the faithless. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish and five were wise.
When the foolish ones took their lamps, they took no oil with them.
But the wise ones took oil with them in their oil flasks along with their lamps.
And as the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and fell asleep.
At midnight there was a cry: 'Look, here is the bridegroom! Come out and go to meet him!'
Then all those virgins got up and trimmed their lamps.
The foolish said to the wise, 'Give us some of your oil too, for our lamps are going out.'
The wise answered them, 'No, there may not be enough for both us and you; go instead to the sellers and buy some for yourselves.'
While they were going off to buy it, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
Afterwards the other virgins came too, saying, 'Lord, lord, open to us!'
But he answered them, 'Truly I tell you, I do not know you.'
Therefore keep watch, for you know neither the day nor the hour.
For it is like a man about to go on a journey, who called his own servants and entrusted his property to them;
To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability, and he went away.
At once the one who had received the five talents went and worked with them, and gained another five.
In the same way, the one who had received two gained another two.
But the one who had received the one talent went and dug in the ground and hid his lord's silver.
After a long time the lord of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
The one who had received the five talents came and brought him another five talents and said to him: "Lord, you gave me five talents; look, I have gained another five talents."
His lord said to him: "Good servant, kind and faithful, you have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your lord."
The one who had received the two talents came forward and said: "Lord, you gave me two talents; look, I have gained two other talents."
His lord said to him: "Good servant, kind and faithful, you have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your lord."
The one who had received one talent came forward and said: "Lord, I knew that you are a harsh man: you reap where you did not sow, and you gather what you did not scatter.
So I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here, you have what is yours."
His lord answered him and said: "Wicked and slothful servant, you knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter;
you ought then to have given my silver to the merchants, and when I came I would have received what is mine with interest.
Now take the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents!
For to everyone who has, more will be given and added, but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
And throw that useless servant into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there."
"When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on the thrones of his glory;
and all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will set the sheep at his right hand and the goats at his left.
Then the King will say to those at his right hand: 'Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom that has been prepared for you from the creation of the world.
For I was hungry and you gave me food; I was thirsty and you gave me drink; I was a stranger and you took me in;
I was naked and you clothed me; I was sick and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me.'
Then the righteous will answer him and say: 'Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you? Or thirsty and give you drink?
Or when did we see you a stranger and take you in? Or naked and clothe you?
When did we ever see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?'
And the King will answer and say to them: "Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these my brothers, you did for me."
Then he will also say to those on the left: "Depart from me, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire that has been prepared for the devil and his servants,
for I was hungry, and you did not give me food; I was thirsty, and you did not give me drink;
I was a stranger, and you did not take me in; I was naked, and you did not clothe me; I was sick and I was in prison, and you did not come to me."
Then they too will answer and say: "Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not serve you?"
He will answer them and say: "Truly I tell you, whenever you did not do it for one of the least of these, you did not do it for me either."
And these will go away into eternal torment, but the righteous into eternal life.
And it happened that when Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples:
"You know that after two days the Passover is to take place, and the Son of Man is to be handed over to be crucified."
Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,
and they took counsel so that they might seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.
And they said: "Not during the festival, so that there may be no uproar among the people."
Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
a woman came to him who had a jar [?] of very costly ointment, and she poured it on his head as he was reclining [?] at table.
When the disciples saw this, they were angered and said: "Why was this ointment wasted?
For it could have been sold for a great sum and given to the poor."
But when Jesus perceived it, he said to them: "Why do you trouble this woman? For she has done a good deed toward me.
The poor are always with you, but I am not always with you.
For in pouring this ointment on my body, she has done it for me in preparation for my burial clothing.
And truly I tell you: wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what this woman has done will also be told, in memory of her."
Then one of the Twelve, whose name was Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said: "What are you willing to give me, and I will hand him over to you?" And they weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.
And from then on he sought a convenient time to hand him over to them.
Now on the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus and said to him: "Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat this Passover?"
And he said to them: "Go into the city to a certain man and say to him: 'The Teacher says this: My time is near; I will keep this Passover at your house with my disciples.'"
And the disciples did as Jesus had commanded them, and they prepared the Passover for him.
And when evening came, he reclined at table with the twelve disciples.
And as they were eating, he said to them: "Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me."
And they were very distressed, and each one began to say: "Surely it is not I, Lord?"
But he answered and said: "The one who dips his hand into the dish with me, he will betray me.
The Son of Man goes, as it is written of him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed. It would have been better for that man if he had not been born."
Judas, who was going to betray him, answered and said: "Surely it is not I, Teacher?" He said to him: "You have said it."
And as they were eating, Jesus took bread and blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples and said: "Take, eat, for this is my body!"
And he took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them and said: "Drink from this, all of you,
for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
But I tell you: from now on I will not drink again of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father."
And after singing a hymn they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus answered and said to them: "All of you will stumble because of me this night, for it is written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.
But when I have risen, I will go ahead of you to Galilee."
Peter answered and said: "Even if all stumble because of you, I will never stumble because of you."
Jesus said to him: "Truly I tell you, this very night, before the cock crows, you will deny me three times."
Peter said to him: "Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you." And all the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus came with them to a village whose name was Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples: "Sit here while I go and pray."
And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and he began to be troubled and grieved.
Then he said to them: "My soul is sorrowful even to death; wait for me here and stay awake with me."
And he went a little farther and fell on his face and prayed and said: "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; yet not as I will, but as you will."
And he came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter: "So you could not stay awake with me for one hour?
Stay awake and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation; the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak."
Then he went a second time, prayed, and said: "My Father, if it is not possible for this cup to pass from me without my drinking it, let your will be done."
And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
And he left them, went away, and prayed a third time, saying the same words again.
Then he came to the disciples and said to them: "Sleep from now on and take your rest. Behold, the hour has come, and the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
Rise, let us go from here. Behold, the one who is handing me over has arrived."
And while he was still saying this, behold, Judas, one of the Twelve, came, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the elders of the people.
Now the one who was handing him over had given them a sign, saying: "The one I kiss is the man. Seize him!"
And at once he came up and said to Jesus: "Greetings, Teacher!" and kissed him.
But Jesus said to him: "Friend, what have you come for?" Then they came up, laid hands on Jesus, and seized him.
And one of those with Jesus reached out his hand, drew his sword, struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him: "Put that sword back in its place, for everyone who takes up the sword will perish by the sword.
Or do you think that I cannot appeal to my Father, and he would now set beside me here more than twelve legions of angels?
And how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?"
At that hour Jesus said to the crowd: "You have come out with swords and clubs to seize me as though against a robber. Every day I sat with you in the temple and taught you, and you did not seize me.
But all this happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled." Then all the disciples left him and fled.
And they seized Jesus and led him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the chief priests and the elders had gathered.
But Peter followed him at a distance to the courtyard of the high priest, and he went inside and sat with the servants to see the outcome.
And the chief priests and the whole council were seeking false testimony against Jesus so that they might put him to death,
and they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. At last two came forward
and said: "This man said, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build it up on the third day.'"
The high priest stood up and said to him: "Do you answer nothing to what these men testify against you?"
But Jesus kept silent. And the high priest said to him: "I put you under oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God."
Jesus said to him: "You have said it. But I tell you: from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven."
Then the high priest tore his garment and said: "He blasphemes! What further need do we have of witnesses? See, you have now heard his blasphemy.
What do you think?" And they answered and said: "He deserves death."
Then they spat in his face and beat him with their fists, and some struck him on the cheek,
and said: "Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?"
Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. And a maidservant came up to him and said: "You too were with Jesus the Galilean."
He denied it before them all and said: "I do not know what you are saying."
And as he went out to the gate, another woman saw him and said to those who were standing there: "This man was with Jesus the Nazarene."
And again he denied it with an oath: "I do not know the man."
And after a little while those who were standing there came up and said to Peter: "Truly you too are one of them, for your speech also makes you known."
Then he began to curse and to swear: "I do not know this man." And immediately a cock crowed.
And he remembered the word of Jesus, who had said to him: "Before the cock crows you will deny me three times." And he went outside and wept bitterly.
And when it dawned, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, to put him to death.
And they bound him and led him away and handed him over to Pilate the governor.
Then Judas, his betrayer, saw that he had been condemned, and he repented and returned the silver to the chief priests and the elders,
and said: "I have sinned, for I have betrayed innocent blood." But they said: "What is that to us? You see to it."
And he threw the silver down in the temple, and went away and [? hanged himself].
But the chief priests took the silver and said: "It is not lawful to put this into the treasury, for it is the price of blood."
They took counsel and with it bought the potter's field, as a burial place for strangers.
For this reason that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
Then was fulfilled the word spoken by Jeremiah the prophet: "And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the precious one, on whom some of the sons of Israel set a price,
and they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord commanded me."
Now Jesus stood before the governor. He questioned him and said: "Are you the king of the Jews?" And Jesus said to him: "You say so."
And when the chief priests and the elders accused him, he answered nothing.
Then Pilate said to him: "Do you not hear how many things they testify against you?"
And he did not answer him even a single word, so that the governor too was greatly amazed.
Now at each feast the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner, whomever they wished.
At that time there was a notorious prisoner, who was called Barabbas.
And when they had gathered together, Pilate said to them: "Which of the two do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?"
For he knew that they had handed him over out of envy.
And as he sat on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him and said: "What is there between you and that righteous man? For I have suffered many things today in a vision because of him."
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and to destroy Jesus.
The governor answered and said to them: "Which of the two do you want me to release to you?" And they said: "Barabbas."
Pilate said to them: "Then what shall I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?" They said to him: "Let him be crucified."
And he said: "What evil has he done?" But they cried out all the more, saying: "Let him be crucified."

When Pilate saw that he was gaining nothing, but rather a greater uproar was arising, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd and said: "I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man; see to it yourselves."
And all the people answered and said: "His blood be on us and on our children."
Then he released Barabbas to them, but Jesus he scourged and handed over to them to be crucified.
Then the governor's soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole band of soldiers around him.
And they stripped him and put a purple cloak on him.
And they made a crown of thorns and set it on his head, and put a reed in his right hand; and they knelt before him and mocked him, saying: "Hail, King of the Jews!"
And they spat on him, and took the reed and struck him on the head.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped the cloak off him and put his own clothing on him, and led him away to be crucified.
And as they were going out, they found a man of Cyrene named Simon. They compelled him to carry his cross.
And they came to the place called Golgotha, which is the Place of the Skull.
And they gave him wine mixed with gall to drink. And when he tasted it, he would not drink.

And when they had crucified him, they divided his garments by lot, so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: "They divided my garments among themselves, and for my tunic they cast lots."
And they sat down there and kept watch over him.
And they placed over his head the charge against him, written: "This is the King of the Jews."
Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.
And those passing by reviled him, wagging their heads
and saying: "O you who would destroy the temple and build it on the third day, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!"
Likewise the chief priests, with the scribes and elders, mocked him and said:
"He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he is the King of the Jews, let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in him.
For he trusted in God; let God deliver him now, if he wants him, for he said: 'I am the Son of God.'"
In the same way the robbers who had been crucified with him also reviled him.
And from the sixth hour darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said: "Eli, Eli! Lama sabachthani?" That is: "God, my God! Why do you forsake me?"
And those who heard it said: "Look, this man is calling for Elijah."
And at once one of them ran and took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink.
But the others said to him: "Wait, let us see whether Elijah comes to save him."
And Jesus cried out with a loud voice and gave up his spirit.
And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth shook, and the rocks were split.
And the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised,
and they came out of the tombs, and after his resurrection they went into the holy city and appeared to many.
And when the centurion and those who were with him keeping watch over Jesus saw the earthquake and what had happened, they were very much afraid and said: "Truly this was the Son of God."
And many women were there, watching from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee to serve him,
among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
And when evening came, a rich man from Arimathea came, whose name was Joseph, for he too had been a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered that it be given to him.
And Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
And he laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock, and he rolled a great stone against the entrance of the tomb and went away.
And Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting in front of the tomb.
On the next day, which is the day after Friday, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate
and said to him: "Lord, we have remembered that that deceiver said while he was still alive: 'On the third day I will rise.'

Therefore order the tomb to be made secure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night and steal him away and say to the people: 'He has risen from the dead.' And the last deception will be worse than the first."
Pilate said to them: "You have a guard. Go and make it secure as you know how."
So they went and made the tomb secure, and sealed the stone, together with the guard.
In the evening of the Sabbath, as it was dawning toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven, came and rolled the stone away from the entrance, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow.
And from fear of him the guards trembled and became like dead men.
The angel answered and said to the women: "Do not be afraid. I know that you are seeking Jesus, who was crucified.
He is not here, but he has risen, as he said. Come and see the place where the Lord lay.
And go quickly and tell his disciples: 'He has risen, and behold, he is going ahead of you to Galilee; there you will see him.' Behold, lo, I have told you."
And they went away very quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy; they ran to tell his disciples.
And behold, Jesus met them and said: "Rejoice!" And they came up to him, took hold of his feet, and worshipped him.
Then Jesus said to them: "Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and there they will see me."
And as they were going, just then some of the guard came into the city and told the chief priests everything that had happened.
And the chief priests gathered together with the elders, took counsel, and gave a large sum of silver to the soldiers
and said to them: "Say this: 'His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were sleeping.'
And if the judge hears of this, we will persuade him and keep you free of trouble."
So they took the silver and did as they had been instructed by them. And this story has spread among the Jews to this very day.
But the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had directed them.
And when they saw him, they worshipped him; but some doubted.
And Jesus came to them, spoke with them, and said: "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. As the Father sent me, so I also send you.
Go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
and teaching them to keep everything that I have commanded you. And behold, lo, I am with you all the days until the end of the world."
